tier_rationale: The device carries exactly one radio, Bluetooth Low Energy, confirmed by its own FCC grant (2AOU6EA01AA1A, 2402-2480 MHz, no WiFi listed) and by nothing else Fellow has filed under that grantee code. A community reverse-engineering project that built a third-party WiFi/Google-Assistant bridge for this kettle establishes, from direct protocol inspection, that the official Fellow app 'connects directly to the kettle over Bluetooth with no intermediary server' and that the bridge exists precisely because the stock device has no cloud path to add voice control or remote scheduling. Core temperature control is also available with no radio at all, via the physical knob on the base. No vendor cloud for this device was found anywhere it would have to appear — the app's own documentation, and the only other Fellow kettle product line with a network stack (the WiFi-based EKG Pro / EKG Updater) is a different radio and a different app that is explicitly incompatible with this model.
the_unplug_test: Turn the knob to a temperature and press the button; the kettle heats regardless of whether a phone, a network, or the internet exists anywhere nearby, because it has no way to reach either. Bluetooth only lets a phone standing next to it, running Fellow's app, do the same thing remotely. Unplugging your router changes nothing here — this kettle was never on your network to begin with.

sources.supports: FCC grant for Fellow Industries, Inc., generic 'Electric Pour-over kettle', granted 2018-02-26, covering Bluetooth only (2402-2480 MHz). No WiFi frequencies appear on the grant, and this is the only FCC ID Fellow Industries holds under grantee code 2AOU6 — the sibling-control check that makes the absence of a WiFi grant meaningful.

Community reverse-engineering project documents the EKG+ as BLE-only and states the official Fellow app 'connects directly to the kettle over Bluetooth' with no server in between; the author built a separate WiFi/Firebase bridge specifically because the stock kettle has no cloud connectivity to add voice-assistant or remote-scheduling features.

Fellow's own current kettle lineup page lists Stagg EKG, Stagg EKG Pro/Pro Studio, and Corvo EKG Pro/Pro Studio, with no 'EKG+' variant present — corroborating that the Bluetooth-only EKG+ has been discontinued from Fellow's current catalog.
Retail listing showing the Stagg EKG+ is still sold as new/legacy stock through third-party channels despite being dropped from Fellow's own current lineup.

open_questions: The Fellow app prompts account creation/login on first use for some Fellow product lines (confirmed for the newer Aiden coffee maker app); whether the legacy EKG+ pairing flow ever required this, versus pairing being purely local BLE with no login gate, was not confirmed directly — the manufacturer's own EKG+-specific support article returned an access-blocked response during this check rather than being read. This does not change the tier, since the reverse-engineering source independently confirms no server is in the command path regardless of any login screen, but it should be nailed down on a future pass.

Whether firmware on this model can ever be updated at all (it predates the WiFi-based EKG Updater app, which is confirmed incompatible with it) — left unknown rather than assumed 'no update mechanism exists'.
Exact discontinuation date not found; only that it is absent from Fellow's current catalog as of this check.
notes: This domain (kitchen) had zero D1 records before this one. The current Fellow lineup replaced EKG+ with the Stagg EKG Pro / Pro Studio, which uses WiFi (not Bluetooth) for firmware checks through the EKG Updater app and would need to be verified separately — do not assume it is also D1, since a WiFi radio checking in with a Fellow server is a materially different fact pattern than this device's BLE-only, server-free design.
